payload.task_text:
Our company is organizing a team-building cooking workshop next month and I need you to prepare the materials. We want to feature three Chinese dishes that are relatively easy to make (rated as easy, i.e. a low difficulty score, in the recipe database), and cover different categories so we get some variety. Please search through the available recipe database to find three suitable dishes that meet these criteria.

Note: write all document content in English (dish names, ingredients, cooking steps, tips, and the shopping list).

Once you have selected the three recipes, I need you to create three deliverables in the workspace.

First, create a Word document called Workshop_Handbook.docx. This should serve as a detailed step-by-step cooking guide for participants. Start with a title "Cooking Workshop Handbook" as a top-level heading. Then for each of the three dishes, include a second-level heading with the dish name, followed by a paragraph listing all the required ingredients with quantities, and then another paragraph (or multiple paragraphs) walking through the cooking steps in order. At the end of the document, add a section called "Tips and Notes" with any general cooking advice that would help beginners.

Second, create a PowerPoint presentation called Workshop_Slides.pptx for the instructor to use during the workshop. The first slide should be a title slide with "Team Cooking Workshop" as the title. Then for each dish, create two slides: one slide with the dish name as the title and the ingredient list as the content, and a second slide with the dish name followed by "Steps" as the title and the cooking steps as bullet points. Finally add a closing slide with "Enjoy Your Meal!" as the title.

Third, create a PDF file called Shopping_List.pdf in the workspace. This should be a consolidated shopping list that combines all ingredients from all three dishes, organized neatly so that someone from our procurement team can use it to go shopping. Group similar ingredients together if possible and include the total quantities needed. The document should have a clear title "Shopping List for Cooking Workshop" at the top.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent must first query the exact `早餐`, `素菜`, and `主食` category listings in one native-parallel response, select one low-difficulty candidate ID from each category, and retrieve the three exact-ID recipe details in a second native-parallel response. Require three distinct IDs/categories and source-supported low difficulty, then freeze each recipe's English name, full translated ingredients with quantities, ordered translated steps, and beginner tips. The three independent deliverables can then be created in one wave.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 3 coder sub-agents in parallel:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): One coder sub-agent owns Workshop_Handbook.docx and writes the exact title, one complete section for each of the three frozen dishes, ordered ingredients/steps, and Tips and Notes. Read it back and return its path and three-dish coverage checks.

   2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 1): One coder sub-agent owns Workshop_Slides.pptx and creates exactly the title slide, two slides for each of the three frozen dishes, and the Enjoy Your Meal closing slide. Read it back and return its path, presentation ID, eight-slide count, titles, and dish coverage.

   3. coder 2 (office-report-builder 2): One coder sub-agent owns Shopping_List.pdf and consolidates all ingredients from the same three frozen recipes in English with combined quantities and clear grouping. Read it back and return its path, title, ingredient coverage, and quantity controls.

After Wave 1, the main agent must cross-check the same three dishes and ingredients across all deliverables and finish without another wave.

Create a Word document at exactly this path:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_Kimi-K3/SingleUserTurn-howtocook-workshop-materials/workspace/Workshop_Handbook.docx

This is a step-by-step cooking guide for a company team-building cooking workshop. ALL content must be in English. Use the mcp__word__ tools (create_document, add_heading, add_paragraph, etc.).

Required structure:
1. A top-level heading (level 1): "Cooking Workshop Handbook"
2. Optionally one short intro paragraph under it (e.g., "Welcome! This handbook guides you through three easy Chinese dishes..."), then for EACH of the three dishes below:
   - A second-level heading (level 2) with the dish name
   - A paragraph (or several) listing ALL required ingredients with quantities
   - Paragraph(s) walking through the cooking steps in order
3. At the end, a second-level heading (level 2): "Tips and Notes", followed by general cooking advice for beginners (provided below).

=== DISH 1 ===
Heading: "Tomato and Egg Stir-fry"
Ingredients paragraph:
"Ingredients (serves 1): 1 tomato (about 180 g); 2 eggs; cooking oil, about 8 ml (roughly 4 ml per egg); salt, 1.5–2 g plus 1 g for the egg mixture; sugar, 0–2 g (optional, for a sweeter version); chopped scallions, 0–10 g (optional)."
Steps (walk through in order, one or more paragraphs):
1. Wash the tomatoes.
2. (Optional) Peel off the tomato skins.
3. Remove the stems and cut the tomatoes into chunks no larger than 4 cm.
4. Crack the eggs into a bowl, add 1 g of salt per serving, and beat until well mixed.
5. Heat the wok over medium-high heat and add the cooking oil.
6. When the oil is hot, pour in the beaten eggs. Stir-fry until the eggs just set and turn slightly golden.
7. Turn off the heat, transfer the eggs to a plate, then turn the heat back on.
8. Add the tomato chunks to the wok. Press them gently with the spatula and stir-fry for about 20 seconds, or until they soften.
9. Return the eggs to the wok and stir-fry everything together.
10. Add the remaining salt, the sugar (optional), and the chopped scallions (optional). Mix well.
11. Turn off the heat and serve.

=== DISH 2 ===
Heading: "Blanched Prawns"
Ingredients paragraph:
"Ingredients (serves 1–2): 250 g live shrimp; 1 onion, cut into small chunks; 1 piece of ginger, sliced; 5–8 garlic cloves, minced (for the dipping sauce); 1 scallion, chopped (for the dipping sauce); 20 ml cooking wine; 10–15 ml soy sauce; 10 ml aromatic vinegar; 10 ml oyster sauce; 10–15 ml cooking oil; a handful of sesame seeds."
Steps:
1. Cut the onion into small chunks and slice the ginger. Spread them evenly over the bottom of a frying pan.
2. Rinse the live shrimp (optionally devein them and trim the legs and whiskers), drain well, and lay them on top of the onion and ginger.
3. Pour the cooking wine into the pan. Cover with a lid and cook on medium heat for 1 minute, then on low heat for 5 minutes. Turn off the heat and let the pan rest, covered, for 5 more minutes.
4. While the shrimp cooks, prepare the dipping sauce: combine the soy sauce, vinegar, oyster sauce, minced garlic, chopped scallion, and sesame seeds in a small bowl. Heat the cooking oil until hot and pour it over the sauce to release the aromas.
5. Transfer the shrimp to a clean plate and serve with the dipping sauce.

=== DISH 3 ===
Heading: "Stir-fried Garlic Sprouts with Minced Pork"
Ingredients paragraph:
"Ingredients (serves 1–2): 1 bunch of garlic sprouts (about 190 g); 4 thin slices of pork belly (about 20 g); 2 garlic cloves; 10 ml cooking oil; 15 ml light soy sauce (divided); 2 g salt; 20 ml water."
Steps:
1. Cut the garlic sprouts into 5 cm segments and set aside.
2. Cut the pork belly into 5 mm × 5 cm strips and set aside.
3. Smash the garlic cloves and mince them; set aside.
4. Heat the wok, add 10 ml of cooking oil, and wait about 10 seconds for the oil to heat up.
5. Add the minced garlic and stir-fry over medium heat for 10 seconds until fragrant.
6. Add the pork and 5 ml of light soy sauce. Stir-fry over medium heat for 30 seconds until the pork is cooked through and lightly colored.
7. Add the garlic sprouts and the remaining 10 ml of light soy sauce. Stir-fry for 30 seconds.
8. Add 20 ml of water and stir-fry over medium heat for 5 minutes, until the garlic sprouts soften slightly.
9. Add 2 g of salt, stir-fry for another 30 seconds, then plate and serve.

=== TIPS AND NOTES SECTION ===
Heading: "Tips and Notes"
Content (as several paragraphs or a list):
- Read the entire recipe before you start cooking.
- Prepare and measure all ingredients before turning on the stove (mise en place).
- Wash all vegetables and proteins before cutting.
- Be careful with hot oil; keep a lid nearby to cover the pan if oil splatters.
- Use medium heat to avoid burning garlic — burnt garlic turns bitter.
- Taste as you go and adjust salt to your preference.
- Keep knives sharp and always cut away from your fingers.
- Fresh live shrimp give the best texture for blanched prawns; fresh chilled shrimp also work.
- Clean as you go to keep your workstation organized and safe.

Deliverable: the file Workshop_Handbook.docx saved at the exact path above, with the heading structure exactly as specified. Verify the document was created (e.g., with get_document_info) before finishing. Report back the file path and a summary of what was written.
Build Workshop_Handbook.docx

This is for the instructor of a company team-building cooking workshop. ALL content must be in English. Use the mcp__pptx__ tools (create_presentation, add_slide, add_bullet_points / populate_placeholder / manage_text, save_presentation).

The deck must contain exactly 8 slides in this order:

SLIDE 1 (title slide): Title = "Team Cooking Workshop" (use a title layout; a subtitle like "Three Easy Chinese Dishes" is optional).

SLIDE 2: Title = "Tomato and Egg Stir-fry". Content = ingredient list as bullet points:
- 1 tomato (about 180 g)
- 2 eggs
- Cooking oil, about 8 ml (4 ml per egg)
- Salt, 1.5–2 g (plus 1 g for the egg mixture)
- Sugar, 0–2 g (optional)
- Chopped scallions, 0–10 g (optional)

SLIDE 3: Title = "Tomato and Egg Stir-fry Steps". Content = cooking steps as bullet points:
- Wash the tomatoes (optionally peel them) and cut into chunks no larger than 4 cm
- Beat the eggs with 1 g of salt per serving
- Heat oil in the wok; pour in the eggs and stir-fry until just set and slightly golden
- Remove the eggs from the wok and set aside
- Add the tomato chunks; press and stir-fry about 20 seconds until soft
- Return the eggs to the wok and mix
- Add the remaining salt, sugar (optional), and scallions (optional); mix well
- Turn off the heat and serve

SLIDE 4: Title = "Blanched Prawns". Content = ingredient list as bullet points:
- 250 g live shrimp
- 1 onion, cut into small chunks
- 1 piece of ginger, sliced
- 5–8 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 scallion, chopped
- 20 ml cooking wine
- 10–15 ml soy sauce
- 10 ml aromatic vinegar
- 10 ml oyster sauce
- 10–15 ml cooking oil
- A handful of sesame seeds

SLIDE 5: Title = "Blanched Prawns Steps". Content = cooking steps as bullet points:
- Spread the onion chunks and ginger slices over the bottom of a frying pan
- Rinse and drain the shrimp (optionally devein and trim); lay them on the onion and ginger
- Pour in the cooking wine; cover and cook 1 minute on medium heat, then 5 minutes on low heat
- Turn off the heat and rest, covered, for 5 minutes
- Meanwhile make the dipping sauce: soy sauce, vinegar, oyster sauce, garlic, scallion, sesame seeds
- Pour hot oil over the sauce to release the aromas
- Plate the shrimp and serve with the dipping sauce

SLIDE 6: Title = "Stir-fried Garlic Sprouts with Minced Pork". Content = ingredient list as bullet points:
- 1 bunch of garlic sprouts (about 190 g)
- 4 thin slices of pork belly (about 20 g)
- 2 garlic cloves
- 10 ml cooking oil
- 15 ml light soy sauce (divided)
- 2 g salt
- 20 ml water

SLIDE 7: Title = "Stir-fried Garlic Sprouts with Minced Pork Steps". Content = cooking steps as bullet points:
- Cut the garlic sprouts into 5 cm segments; cut the pork into 5 mm × 5 cm strips; mince the garlic
- Heat 10 ml of oil in the wok for about 10 seconds
- Stir-fry the minced garlic on medium heat for 10 seconds until fragrant
- Add the pork and 5 ml of light soy sauce; stir-fry 30 seconds until cooked and colored
- Add the garlic sprouts and the remaining 10 ml of light soy sauce; stir-fry 30 seconds
- Add 20 ml of water; stir-fry on medium heat for 5 minutes until the sprouts soften slightly
- Add 2 g of salt; stir-fry 30 seconds, then plate and serve

SLIDE 8 (closing slide): Title = "Enjoy Your Meal!" (a short line like "Thank you for cooking with us!" is optional).

Keep each slide readable: use bullet points for content slides; do not overcrowd. Save the file to the exact path above and verify with get_presentation_info before finishing. Report back the file path and the slide count.
Build Workshop_Slides.pptx

Create a PDF file at exactly this path:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_Kimi-K3/SingleUserTurn-howtocook-workshop-materials/workspace/Shopping_List.pdf

This is a consolidated shopping list for a company cooking workshop, to be used by the procurement team. ALL content must be in English. The document must have a clear title "Shopping List for Cooking Workshop" at the top.

It combines all ingredients from three dishes: Tomato and Egg Stir-fry, Blanched Prawns, and Stir-fried Garlic Sprouts with Minced Pork. Group similar ingredients together and include total quantities.

Content (use these exact groups and items; quantities are totals across all three dishes):

Fresh Produce
- Tomatoes: 1 (about 180 g)
- Garlic sprouts: 1 bunch (about 190 g)
- Onion: 1
- Ginger: 1 piece (about 20 g)
- Garlic: 1 whole head (7–10 cloves)
- Scallions (spring onions): 2 stalks

Meat & Seafood
- Live shrimp: 250 g
- Pork belly: 4 thin slices (about 20 g)

Eggs
- Eggs: 2

Pantry & Condiments
- Cooking oil: about 30 ml (1 small bottle)
- Salt: about 5 g
- Sugar: about 2 g (optional)
- Soy sauce: 10–15 ml
- Light soy sauce: 15 ml
- Cooking wine: 20 ml
- Oyster sauce: 10 ml
- Aromatic vinegar: 10 ml
- Sesame seeds: 1 handful (about 10 g)

You may add a short note line at the bottom such as: "Quantities cover one batch of each dish (serves about 4–6 people in total). Scale up as needed for your group size."

Recommended approach: use the mcp__word__ tools to create a nicely formatted document with the title as a top-level heading, each group as a second-level heading, items as a list or table, then use mcp__word__convert_to_pdf to produce Shopping_List.pdf at the exact path above (then remove/ignore the intermediate .docx, or keep it — but the PDF must exist). If convert_to_pdf fails, fall back to generating the PDF with mcp__local__python_execute (try fpdf2 first: `from fpdf import FPDF`; if unavailable try reportlab). Make sure text is legible and the layout is neat and organized.

Verify the final PDF exists at the exact path above (e.g., via filesystem get_file_info) before finishing. Report back the file path and how it was generated.
Build Shopping_List.pdf
